lines: Your car won't start, and the repair costs 450 dollars. With an emergency fund, it's an annoying day. Without one, it goes on a credit card and grows with interest.
An emergency fund is savings you only use for something needed, urgent and unexpected. A repair you need for work counts. Concert tickets don't. Neither do bills you know are coming.
Size it by your monthly needs: rent, food, gas and phone. Yours add up to 1,200 dollars a month.
Most planners suggest three to six months of needs. Three months is 3,600 dollars. Aim for six if your pay changes a lot or you're the only income at home.
Start with a first goal of 400 dollars. In a 2025 Federal Reserve survey, only 63 percent of adults could cover a 400 dollar surprise with cash.
Saving 480 dollars a month, the full 3,600 takes 7.5 months. Set up an automatic transfer on payday.
Keep it in a separate, FDIC-insured savings account. Not in stocks, which can drop right when you need the money.
When the fund is full, it covers three months with no paycheck. After you use it, refill it before other goals. 450 dollars takes about one month to refill.
A camel's hump is stored fat. In hard times the camel lives on it and the hump shrinks. In good times it fills back up. Your fund works the same way.
